newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Last batch of Nigerian Shell hostages freed.
newsitem.headline: Last batch of Nigerian Shell hostages freed.

text.p: The last batch of Shell oil workers held hostages by villagers in Nigeria were freed on Thursday, a company spokesman said.

"All our staff and contractors are now back safely in Warri," said the Shell spokesman in Lagos, referring to the midwestern oil city of Warri that is headquarters of Shell's operations in the western sector of Nigeria.

The hostage saga began last Saturday when Ijaw tribesmen protesting the relocation of their local government headquarters to another town occupied six flow stations of Shell on which they detained 127 staff and contractors, all of them Nigerians.
Negotiations secured the release of the hostages in batches and by Thursday there were 52 still held and community leaders pledged that they would be released later in the day.
The Shell spokesman said there had been no conditions set by the villagers for freeing the company's staff. "All they asked was that we should pass on their grievances to the government."

Three Ijaw tribesmen have died in the protests that escalated into riots in Warri on Tuesday and forced the reduction in Shell's oil output in the area. Output has also been cut in Nembe in the southeast, where villagers protesting against the merger of two communities into one local government also seized Shell flow stations and ordered its staff out of the facility.
